questions.stem: In the reaction 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO, what is the mole ratio of magnesium to magnesium oxide?
questions.explanation: The coefficients show that 2 moles of Mg produce 2 moles of MgO. This simplifies to a 1:1 ratio - each mole of magnesium produces one mole of magnesium oxide.

questions.stem: In the reaction CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂, what mass of CaO is produced from 100 g of CaCO₃? [Mr: CaCO₃ = 100, CaO = 56]
questions.explanation: 100 g of CaCO₃ = 100/100 = 1 mole. The equation shows 1 mole of CaCO₃ produces 1 mole of CaO. Mass of 1 mole CaO = 56 g.

questions.stem: What is the first step in a reacting masses calculation?

options.text: Write a balanced equation for the reaction
Calculate the volume of gas produced

questions.explanation: The first step is always to write a balanced chemical equation. This gives you the mole ratios needed to relate the amounts of different substances in the reaction.

questions.stem: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂. How many moles of H₂ are produced from 4 moles of Na?
questions.explanation: The equation shows 2 moles of Na produce 1 mole of H₂. So 4 moles of Na (double) will produce 2 moles of H₂ (double).

questions.stem: What mass of oxygen reacts with 48 g of magnesium? 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO [Ar: Mg = 24, O = 16]
questions.explanation: 48 g Mg = 48/24 = 2 moles Mg. From the equation, 2 moles Mg reacts with 1 mole O₂. Mass of 1 mole O₂ = 32 g.

questions.stem: Why are mole ratios important in reacting mass calculations?

options.text: They tell you the temperature of the reaction
They show the proportions in which substances react and are produced
They indicate the colour of the products
They determine the speed of the reaction

questions.explanation: Mole ratios from balanced equations show the proportions in which reactants combine and products form. This allows you to calculate how much of one substance reacts with or is produced from another.

questions.stem: In the reaction Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂, how many moles of iron are produced from 1 mole of Fe₂O₃?
questions.explanation: The balanced equation shows 1 mole of Fe₂O₃ produces 2 moles of Fe. The coefficient 2 in front of Fe tells us the mole ratio.
